acceptanceCriteria: internal/testvalidity reports ISOLATED-IN-SERIAL for an isolated test under a describe.configure({mode:'serial'}) ancestor and under test.describe.serial, naming the ancestor file:line; synthetic fixtures cover both forms and a non-serial negative
A test without an isolation annotation under a serial suite is not reported (negative fixture)
The rule has a numbered requirement and traceability row in the test-validity spec
If the optional serial-skip summary is not delivered, a follow-up ticket records it
body: GitHub issue #1123. A test annotated isolated (own seed/session) can sit inside a describe configured with mode serial (or test.describe.serial). A failure of an earlier serial test skips it, so a targeted witness run reports skipped and proves nothing. Expected: a test-validity rule ISOLATED-IN-SERIAL reports any test carrying an isolation annotation (or creating its own fixture data and session) under a serial ancestor, naming the serial ancestor's file:line and suggesting moving the test out or dropping serial mode. Optional: runner summary distinguishes skipped-because-earlier-serial-test-failed from a plain skip, naming the failing test.
title: test-validity: flag isolated tests nested in a serial suite, ISOLATED-IN-SERIAL (#1123)
